stages.description: You, a tone probe, a clipboard and the frame.
A junior technician does the house installs and the frame work from your handwritten job sheets, one customer a day.
stages.newProblem: Their mistakes look fine today and surface weeks later.

stages.description: Job tickets live in a database; the tech can see which pairs are already faulty.
stages.newProblem: When the database is wrong, everyone is wrong together.

stages.description: Remote provisioning. Customers are switched on from a screen.
stages.newProblem: When provisioning breaks, it breaks for every new customer at once.

stages.description: Carbon-copy invoices at the kitchen table.
A part-time bookkeeper and a shoebox of receipts.
stages.newProblem: The bookkeeper notices things. All of the things.

stages.description: Billing software on a green-screen terminal.
A billing platform with revenue graphs.
stages.newProblem: Vendor lock-in. The vendor knows it.

stages.description: An answering machine and your own voice, hoarse by Friday.
A receptionist with a notebook of common faults.
stages.newProblem: Calls you used to hear now arrive as summaries.

stages.description: A ticket system. Every complaint has a number.
stages.newProblem: Tickets can be closed without being solved.
People who need a human can no longer find one.

stages.description: Drive out, listen to the line, find the fault with your hands.
A field tech dispatched from a terminal showing alarm lights.
stages.newProblem: The terminal shows symptoms, not causes.

stages.description: Alarm correlation in a network operations centre.
stages.newProblem: The first automated failure is small, embarrassing, and a warning.
